docs.text: Cactuses in northern Indiana! Growing wild in the sand alongside dune grasses, these “Eastern Prickly Pear” were about 200 meters from Lake Michigan. Saw some here last June with yellow flowers—these October ones have fruit. Seeing cactuses growing in coastal Indiana kind of makes me happy.

Well, we are surrounded by Great Lakes here in Michigan, don't know if that would make it easier for it to grow here? You do see a lot of stuff like it around here all over trees and poles along highways, but that one stands out in the city. It's been like that at the road into Hamtramck for years

Wow! This was so new to me, I can barely picture how it grows. Cacti are like palm trees, things that I know exist but I can barely believe in them. I live in maple and beech country, at the edge of the Great Lakes where summers are hot and winters are (usually) cold. Cacti are fascinating to me.
Haha maybe. I’m still trying to figure out how a coconut winds up along the shore of Lake Michigan. Who brings a whole, unbroken coconut to a picnic?

And cacti!
I was so surprised to see the cacti next to Lake Michigan.
I went to visit the local cactus by the lake yesterday.
A prickly pear cactus growing in the sand dunes along Lake Michigan!

I've always wondered why the Lake Michigan beaches in Chicago didn't have coconut trees to grow our own food. Now I've learned it's because we've turned away from the Bible. Of course! What other possible answer could there be? Praise Jesus! Unless he's snatched by masked ICE agents.

beautiful! my Ontario Cactus has bright light yellow flowers.
yes Ontario has a native cactus. grows native only on a very small area on the shore of Lake Ontario. Has been doing amazing in pots in front of house for years.
I just found a coconut washed up on the shore of lake Ontario.
